title: AA Batteries 8-pack

drivers.name: Price increase (5.5%)
drivers.evidence: Recent weeks at $10.81 (vs $10.25) averaged 31.5 units vs baseline 34.9: x0.90. No promotions or events. Price hike likely reduces demand.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 34.9. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price is 5.5% above regular, which historically correlates with lower demand: recent weeks at $10.81 show median sales of 31.5 vs baseline 34.9 (x0.90). The heatwave (38°C) may drive demand for battery-powered cooling devices, but no evidence links heat to sales spikes. Past promotions at similar price points show noise-adjusted uplift of x1.17; here, a price increase likely suppresses demand. The classical model suggests no uplift, but judgment overrides it: price increase is a clear demand reducer. No other drivers. Adjust down modestly.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 34.9 | 5%-95%: 18.5 - 58.2 | 10%-90%: 20.9 - 55.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-44% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
